project.name: Auchmithie
project.boundarySource: Mapped named-place location with a conservative editorial study buffer
project.researchNotes: Full strict-boundary visitor audit. Auchmithie qualifies on its own village character, shore, harbour, Smokie heritage and destination food stop. Ethie Castle, Arbroath, St Vigeans and other nearby merit are excluded. Castle Rock scheduled fort remains catalogued but map-hidden because no defensible construction period is present in the local HES record. No dedicated Treasure Trails, Curious About, Mystery Guides or Go Quest product was found for Auchmithie; official council and VisitAngus routes are retained. Parking charges are unknown unless explicitly published. Angus-wide full audit completed 2026-09-01: all six visitor categories, the four named commercial trail providers, current official/conventional routes, strict-boundary scoring and local HES/NRHE integrity were checked.

touristAppeal.label: Great Choice
touristAppeal.summary: A genuinely distinctive clifftop fishing village with dramatic beach and cave scenery, the old harbour, nationally resonant Smokie heritage, three verified trail resources and a destination lunch or high-tea stop.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: Outdoor coast and village walks suit responsible dogs, but steep steps, exposed cliff edges, livestock risk and unconfirmed indoor access require planning.

visitorHighlights.name: Auchmithie Beach, Cliffs and Caves
visitorHighlights.reason: A dramatic, distinctive and officially promoted Angus coast experience that independently justifies a visit, tempered by steep access and erosion risk.
visitorHighlights.tagline: Cliffs, caves and secluded pebble shore
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Outdoor access; avoid cliff edges and check tide, weather and erosion warnings

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A dramatic, distinctive and officially promoted Angus coast experience that independently justifies a visit, tempered by steep access and erosion risk.

visitorHighlights.name: Auchmithie Old Harbour and Smokie Heritage
visitorHighlights.reason: A compact but nationally resonant fishing-heritage stop, strengthened by the surviving harbour setting and official Smokie Trail interpretation.
visitorHighlights.tagline: Fishing harbour at the Smokie’s birthplace
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Outdoor access; lower shore route is steep

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A compact but nationally resonant fishing-heritage stop, strengthened by the surviving harbour setting and official Smokie Trail interpretation.

townGuide.characterTag: Smokie heritage above dramatic sandstone cliffs
townGuide.headline: A small fishing village that earns its coastal detour
townGuide.intro: Auchmithie is more than a gateway to a nearby attraction: its cliff-top setting, steep shore, old harbour, Smokie origin story and destination food stop combine into a coherent half-day visit.
bestFor: A cliff walk with lunch or high tea
perfectFor: Combining scenery with a distinctive daytime meal

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Cliffs, harbour and Smokie heritage
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Park in the village, pause at the cliff-top viewpoint, descend only if conditions suit, explore the old harbour setting and finish at But ’n’ Ben.

dontMiss: The pebble shore and sandstone cliffs
Old harbour and Smokie Trail stop
townGuide.suggestedTime: 2–4 hours; around 4 hours more for a return walk to Arbroath
townGuide.visitorMood: Small and exposed but highly distinctive, with enough independent village content to justify its own map score.

White-painted harl and black-painted margins and cills. Slate roof, raised block skewputts and end stacks.
